pages.title: Chen Huang
pages.text: He who rides it shall live two thousand years. The Chen Huang of the ancient texts resembles a four-horned deer clad in starlit scales, the swiftest of all divine beasts. Lost travelers borne by a Chen Huang could cross an entire wilderness in a single day.

pages.title: Tale
pages.text: In the earliest age, when heaven and earth had just settled, starlight fell into the wilderness and congealed into a four-horned deer. Its hooves never touched the dust; where it passed, mountains and rivers shrank into distant shadows within a single day — distances mortals chase for a lifetime are but a morning stroll to it. $(br)The ancient texts record: he who rides it shall live two thousand years. To a lost traveler borne by a Chen Huang, a way home was granted; and so the ancients revered it as an auspicious beast. Later the starlight faded, and the Chen Huang withdrew into legendary mountains, leaving behind only a few scattered words — swift as a shooting star — and a speed and endurance far beyond mortal limits.
